Emma / team — I ran three concise scenarios against the spreadsheet you shared. High-level assumptions are in the attached notes; I pulled out the core numbers here for clarity.

Scenario 1 — Commitment-first (12B/month):
- Commit: 12B tokens/mo (monthly charge $X)
- Unit price inside commit: $0.75 / 1k tokens (example)
- Burst routing: up to 36B additional tokens/month to buffer at $1.50 / 1k (capped at buffer size)
- True-up: annual true-up if 12B average significantly > committed; unused committed capacity does not rollover (can discuss rollover).

Scenario 2 — Smaller commit + larger prepaid buffer:
- Commit: 6B tokens/mo
- Unit price inside commit: $0.90 / 1k tokens
- Prepaid buffer: 30B credits purchased upfront at $1.10 / 1k tokens usable for bursts; unused credits can be credited toward next year at 50% face value or rolled for 3 months.

Scenario 3 — No hard commit (banded consumption):
- No minimum commit; tiered per-1k pricing that steps down at 10B, 25B, 50B monthly consumption bands. Predictability is lower but we can include a 15% monthly overrun cap that triggers outreach before spend exceeds expectations.

Overrun protection options (add-ons):
- Cap & Amortize: set a hard monthly cap on billable spend above which we pause usage or switch to a throttled fallback; overages within cap are amortized across next 3 months.
- Escrowed Credits: Customer prepays X tokens worth of credits as an insurance buffer. Credits are used during spikes and replenish capability is discussed at renewal.
- Auto-Fallback: during sustained spikes we automatically route to a lower-cost model variant to avoid runaway spend (requires agreement on acceptable quality delta).

I'll attach a short cost sheet and a sample monthly invoice mock that shows how true-ups and amortization would appear.

Emma — thanks for the prompt review. Based on your usage curve the approach I recommend is a hybrid: 9–12B committed baseline + a 25B prepaid buffer purchased at a mid-tier rate with a 6-month rollover and a 90-day replenishment trigger. Operational notes below: 

- Billing visibility: CloudShop will receive token-level aggregation daily plus a weekly burn forecast; we will send a proactive spike alert at 60% of prepaid buffer (and again at 85%).
- Buffer handoff: bursts are first consumed from buffer (no throttling), then once buffer exhausted we throttle non-critical traffic to variant model or apply the capped overrun price.
- True-up mechanics: at annual renewal we reconcile actual annualized consumption vs committed spend. If CloudShop consumed > committed, the overage is billed at committed marginal rate; if actual < committed, credits are applied toward next term (or refunded per negotiated refund schedule).
- Security/compliance: hosted API access will remain in Redwood's multi-tenant hosted environment; if you need Private/VPC deployment we can provide a parallel quote.

Next steps: Vanessa, I suggest we propose a concrete term sheet (9B commit, 25B buffer, 12-month term) for CloudShop to review. Emma — want to schedule a 30-min commercial handoff this week so procurement can validate the buffer mechanism?
